our_interpretation: The phase-one deadline is December 31, 2028, the latest date meant by sometime in 2028.
I read opens in the decade clause as completion of the full campus. Reading it as first operation would conflict with the preceding discussion of phased delivery.
Even if construction has begun is a concession, not an assertion that groundbreaking occurred or a prerequisite for the forecast.
The decade clause expressly assumes a sustained build rate of 800MW every two years. That assumption must be distinguished from an observed construction rate.
Difficulty is not synonymous with missing a deadline. Timely delivery could still involve substantial difficulty.
criteria.support_condition: Records establish substantial difficulty delivering approximately 800MW by the end of 2028. For the full-campus clause, records also establish the stipulated construction rate and completion more than ten years after construction began.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Records establish timely phase-one delivery without substantial difficulty, or full-campus completion within ten years while the stipulated rate and capacity definitions apply. Faster construction would invalidate the assumed rate rather than contradict the conditional arithmetic.
